text:
jen_s: Support escalation — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spike after runtime 2.1.7 rollout in us-west-2. Affects /v1/generate, redwood-ggml-3b. p99 ~3x baseline, began ~09:12 UTC. Can someone own triage? :eyes:

ben_support: Thanks Jen. Can you drop the dashboard link and one failing request id? Also which cohorts (canary vs prod) saw it first?

jen_s: Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/abc123 (p95/p99 panels). Failed req sample: req_id=7f4b2a. Canary cohort showed a small bump at 09:10, prod started rising at 09:12 after routing ramp.

maya_r: Noted. Was canary rollout fully green? Do we have canary audit logs?

deploy-bot: Canary health check: runtime/2.1.7 canary -> 3 hosts. health: OK. latency_anomaly: detected at 09:10 in cohort A.

sean_sre: Ok. First checks: host iowait, CPU steal, and queueing metrics. Also check kernel-selector flag in 2.1.7 — that changed scheduling behavior in small batches.

alice_rt: If we need quick mitigation, we can route the traffic back to runtime/2.1.6 for affected tenants. Example config snippet to update route: 
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "traffic": {"runtime/2.1.6": 100}
}
```

ben_support: Trying traffic-split rollback for acme-inc and co. Running CLI: `redwood route update --tenant acme-inc --route /v1/generate --to runtime/2.1.6`

deploy-bot: Traffic change applied to tenant=acme-inc, route=/v1/generate -> runtime/2.1.6 (immediate).

maya_r: Good. Can we also increase trace sampling to 100% for affected tenants for next 10m so we get full spans?

jen_s: Trace sampling bumped for acme-inc and two other tenants.

ben_support: Quick logs from req_id=7f4b2a: ```
queue_wait_ms=1200
decode_ms=30
kernel_wait_ms=1150
kv_cache_miss=false
```

alice_rt: kernel_wait_ms high — suggests scheduler/late-binding latency rather than model decode. What's KV cache miss rate for this tenant?

ben_support: KV cache miss rate ~5% (normal). So not cache miss flood.

maya_r: That points at the kernel selector change. 2.1.7 introduced `adaptive-kernel-selector` that switches kernels on cold sequences — maybe causing context switch long tail under certain batch patterns. We should bisect the canary commits to confirm. I'll list the suspect commits.

maya_r: Suspect range: commit range abc1234..def5678. Key commits: abc1234 (scheduler tweak), bcd2345 (kv cache metric), cde3456 (kernel selector refactor), def5678 (telemetry).

sean_sre: I'll run a bisect using the canary config toggles to flip `adaptive-kernel-selector` on/off per host and watch p99. Command I'm using: 
```bash
for host in host1 host2 host3; do ssh $host sudo sysctl runtime.adaptive_kernel=0; sleep 60; done
# then observe p99 in Prometheus
```

deploy-bot: Scheduled job started: bisect-toggle-adaptive-kernel (hosts: host1,host2,host3).

sean_sre: Update — toggled adaptive_kernel=0 on host2 only (canary subset). p99 for canary cohort dropped ~40% within 30s. Reverted host2 -> 0 back to 1, p99 rose back. Re-applied 0 to host1+host3 -> p99 returned near baseline.

maya_r: That pretty strongly implicates the kernel selector refactor (commit cde3456). Recommend we push a hotfix to set `adaptive_kernel=false` by default in the runtime config for 2.1.7 and rerun rollout.

alice_rt: Agreed. I'll prepare a canary config override patch and apply at 25% then monitor p95/p99 for 15 min. Patch will be: 
```yaml
runtime_flags:
  adaptive_kernel: false
```

ben_support: Notifying customers now: "We've identified a regression tied to a new scheduling heuristic in the latest runtime. We're rolling a mitigation and will follow up with a timeline." :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Patch applied to runtime/2.1.7 canary override (25% hosts). Monitoring p95/p99.

jen_s: Early numbers: canary p99 back to ~1.1x baseline, prod shows downward trend where traffic split was applied.

sean_sre: I'll keep the bisect job running to gather more granular data and prepare a rollback plan if the patch doesn't hold. If stable for 30m, we can resume rollout with the flag disabled or revert commit cde3456 and re-release.

maya_r: Add note to postmortem: include repro steps (toggle sysctl on hosts), span logs showing kernel_wait_ms, and the bisect commands. Also add alert threshold to catch kernel_wait_ms > 500ms.

ben_support: Customer msgs queued, will update once we have a final fix. Thanks all.

jen_s: Thanks team — looks like mitigation working. Please leave summary + timeline in #postmortems when stable. Closing escalation for now. :tada:
